priceSnapshot.note: Price is 76,785.3. Against the 78,945.5 close of the 17:45Z fifteen-minute bar on 14 September - a true rolling 24 hours - that is 2,160.2 points and 2.74 percent lower. Against today's 00:00Z open of 78,195.7 it is 1,410.4 points and 1.80 percent lower. Against the morning session's 76,959.9 mark it is only 174.6 points and 0.23 percent lower, and that near-flat number hides the largest intraday range of the month: price fell 1,356.9 points from the morning mark to 75,603.0 at 14:45Z, then rallied 1,745.9 points to 77,348.9 at 17:30Z, and has settled back into the middle. Both of the morning report's downside markers were taken out on the way down - the 76,704.0 reduce gate on a settled 1H close and the 76,394.9 invalidation on price - and both have since been reclaimed. This report is written from that fact rather than around it.

reduceIf.confirmation: A settled 1H CLOSE below 76,192.6, the low of the current 17:00Z hour and 592.7 points under the mark. That level is chosen rather than today's 75,603.0 low because the 75,603.0 print lasted four minutes and was bought; 76,192.6 is where the recovery hour began, so a settled close beneath it says the V-shaped reclaim has failed on its own terms rather than merely been retested. On that close, reduce the spot core a second time and hold the cash through the FOMC rather than trying to catch the 75,603.0 retest.

addIf.confirmation: A settled 1H CLOSE above 77,118.5, the 1H EMA20, which sits 6.2 points from the daily EMA20 at 77,112.3 - the tightest confluence of the two most-watched averages this month. Price closed below the daily EMA20 for the first time since 3 September on today's action, so reclaiming that six-point band on an hourly close is the minimum evidence that the break was a wick rather than a change of regime. The gate is 413.4 points LOWER than the morning set it, because the 1H EMA20 itself has fallen 413.4 points; the level is being tracked, not loosened.

decisionBox.changed: Position moves from ADD to REDUCE, and the trigger for the change is the morning report's own instruction rather than a new opinion. The morning set a 76,704.0 reduce gate requiring a settled 1H close and wrote: on that close, stop the staged accumulation and hold the remaining cash into the FOMC. The 13:00Z bar closed 76,620.6 at 14:00Z - 83.4 points through - and the 14:00Z bar confirmed at 75,938.8, 765.2 points through. The 76,394.9 invalidation was then breached on price by 791.9 points at the 75,603.0 low. The gate fired on its terms and the invalidation broke, so the staged accumulation stops here and part of what was bought comes back off. Three further things argue for taking risk down rather than merely pausing. First, the bounce is short-covering, not demand: the entire visible liquidation feed - 100 fills, 1,156,761 USD, 15:24:51Z to 16:20:19Z - is SHORT liquidations between 76,312.0 and 76,565.5, so the 1,745.9-point rally was forced buying from the other side of the book, and the fuel is now spent. Second, the crowd is leaning the wrong way and leaning harder: the OKX long-short account ratio has climbed 1.24 to 1.84 since 00:00Z with funding positive at 0.00741 percent, which is the condition the 13 September midnight lesson names as the disqualifier for treating a flush as a floor. Third, the macro that caused the move has not resolved - Brent is up 3.34 percent to 109.21 on the Saudi pipeline closure and the US 10-year printed a 19-year high at 5.041 percent - with an FOMC tomorrow. Cash is the position that gets paid if any of those three break the wrong way.

liquidation.note: 611,242 USD across 47 fills - SHORT liquidations, buy-side, and the largest measured cluster in the feed, now 385.3 points below the mark. It contains two of the three biggest prints of the window: 270.56 contracts at 76,465.3 (about 206,885 USD) at 15:25:48Z and 200.44 contracts at 76,425.4 (about 153,187 USD) at 15:25:29Z. This is the fuel that produced the 1,745.9-point rally and it has already been burned - the shorts that were carried out here are gone. Marked as the magnet because it is the largest measured level and the one price gravitates back toward if the squeeze unwinds, NOT because there is fresh fuel resting there.

501,457 USD across 42 fills - short liquidations 485.3 points below the mark, including the single largest print in the window at 240.91 contracts on 76,319.0 (about 183,860 USD) at 15:24:51Z, which is where the squeeze started. Together with the 76,400 shelf this is 1,112,699 USD - 96.2 percent of all measured force-closing - inside a 56-minute window.

44,062 USD across 11 fills - short liquidations 285.3 points below the mark, printed last at 16:20:19Z. Small, and useful mainly as the marker of where the forced buying stopped: no contract has been liquidated in either direction in the 85 minutes since.

liquidityMagnet.note: nearestAbove is null and that is a measurement limit, not a claim that nothing sits above. The OKX filled-liquidation feed is capped at 100 fills and today's short squeeze consumed every one of them, so the long liquidations that certainly printed during the 75,603.0 flush are no longer inside the window and cannot be quantified from this feed. What CAN be verified is the direction of the pull, and it points down on two independent readings: the only measured clusters are below price, and the long-short account ratio has risen from 1.24 at 00:00Z to 1.84 at 17:00Z - the most crowded the long side has been this month - while funding stayed positive at 0.00741 percent, so longs are both crowded and paying to stay. The forward heatmap that would fill the gap above needs a keyed CoinGlass source; the browser fallback was not used this run because the free OKX feed returned fresh data rather than being blocked.

RSI bottomed at 20.31 on the 14:30Z bar and at 21.74 on the 14:45Z bar that printed the 75,603.0 low, and is now 55.57 - a 35-point repair in three hours. The MACD histogram has flipped positive to plus 79.53 with the line at minus 76.05 still under a minus 155.58 signal, which is the shape of a momentum low rather than a momentum top. Price is 250.0 points above the EMA20 and 63.0 below the EMA50, so it has reclaimed the fastest average and is fighting the next one. No divergence: the 75,603.0 low was a lower low on a LOWER RSI than the morning's 76,704.0 low at 22.22, which is confirmation of the sell-off, not a hidden bid.

scalpContext.intradayBias: A 1,745.9-point range from 75,603.0 to 77,348.9 that price has settled into the middle of, 1,182.3 points above the low and 563.6 below the high. Above, the 77,112.3 daily EMA20 and 77,118.5 hourly EMA20 form a six-point wall 333.2 points up - the single most important number on the chart today. Below, the 76,400 liquidation shelf is 385.3 points away and the 76,192.6 hour low 592.7. 15m RSI at 55.57 with a positive histogram argues against shorting into the middle of a V; 1H RSI at 43.75 with the histogram at minus 77.39 argues against buying it. Trade the 77,118.5 reclaim or the 76,192.6 break, and nothing in between - the FOMC is tomorrow and the ranges are 2.5 times a normal session.

etfFlows.note: Farside Investors US spot Bitcoin ETF tape, re-read at 12:35 COT. No 15 September row exists yet - US flows publish after the close - so 14 September remains the last complete row at plus 159.9 million: IBIT plus 134.3, FBTC plus 53.3, MSBT plus 9.7, EZBC plus 4.6, ARKB minus 42.0, everything else flat. The positive streak is one session long and it ended a four-session outflow run of 08 to 11 September totalling minus 462.7 million. The distinction the midnight session drew still holds and is sharper today: the 159.9 million that came in through the ETF wrapper is unlevered and cannot be liquidated, while 1,156,761 USD of leveraged shorts were force-closed this afternoon and an unmeasurable amount of leveraged longs before them. One is a floor, the other is a mechanism.

indices.bias: Cheap and getting cheaper in real time. QQQ's last settled close is still Monday 14 September at 709.18, and the session now in progress is trading 704.78, down another 4.40 and 0.62 percent, with the day's range 703.91 to 709.53 on 14.7 million shares at 1:46 PM EDT. That live print is BELOW the 706.32 bottom of the trailing month used for the zone calculation, so the 12th percentile carried below is, if anything, generous - on today's action the Nasdaq proxy is making a new one-month low. The driver is legible and it is the same one hitting bitcoin: the US 10-year printed 5.041 percent, a 19-year high, and Brent jumped 3.34 percent to 109.21 on the Saudi pipeline closure. Long-duration growth carries a rate shock first. For a monthly contribution the advice does not change from midnight or morning: this is a contribution, not a trade, and there is no reason to front-run tomorrow's FOMC to place it.

JPXN's last settled close is Monday 14 September at 104.34, down 0.44 percent, and it sits at the 84th percentile of its trailing month, 1.36 percent ABOVE its 20-day average and only 0.60 percent off the month's high with RSI at 58.99 - rich, where the two US funds are cheap. The mechanism that had been supporting it is turning: a stronger dollar helps Japanese exporters in yen terms, but Brent at 109.21 hurts a net energy importer more than it helps its exporters, and today oil is the bigger move. For a monthly DCA the implication is unchanged - contribute the minimum here or skip it this month, not because the trend is wrong but because the entry is poor relative to its own recent range.

calibration.rollingRecord: Gates over the six publications from 14 September morning through 15 September morning: 2 reduce fired of 6, 4 adds fired of 6. Discretionary calls over the same six: 4 green, 2 red. The 15 September midday session is still open on both counts and is counted in neither figure.
calibration.note: The morning session set a 76,704.0 reduce gate and a 77,531.9 add gate at 12:07Z. The REDUCE GATE FIRED and fired fast. It required a settled 1H close below 76,704.0; the 13:00Z bar closed 76,620.6 at 14:00Z, clearing by 83.4 points, and the 14:00Z bar confirmed at 75,938.8, clearing by 765.2. Four consecutive settled hourly closes printed beneath it - 76,620.6, 75,938.8, 76,505.7, 76,383.9 - before the live 17:00Z bar at 76,867.4 recovered it. The 76,394.9 INVALIDATION was BREACHED on price at 14:45Z, the 75,603.0 low clearing it by 791.9 points, though no settled hourly close printed below it (the lowest was 75,938.8, 456.9 points above). The 77,531.9 add gate did NOT fire: the session high of 77,348.9 came 183.0 points short and no settled close printed above 76,948.3. No resting stop was recommended - stopOrder.recommended was false - and one WOULD have been valuable: the 76,650.0 price the morning carried in the unrecommended stopOrder field was cleared by 1,047.0 points. That is the fourth time in five sessions the stop decision mattered and the first time declining it cost anything material. Morning published range with a BEARISH tilt at 34 bear against 25 bull and price is 174.6 points and 0.23 percent lower, so the tilt was right in direction and almost meaningless in size - which understates how right it was, because the path ran 1,356.9 points in the tilt's favour before retracing. Discretionary: morning ADDED an 8.00 USDT spot tranche at 76,959.9 on top of the midnight session's 12.00 USDT at 76,994.5. Spot marks 76,785.3, so the morning tranche is 174.6 points and 0.23 percent offside (about minus 0.02 USDT) and the midnight tranche 209.2 points and 0.27 percent offside (about minus 0.03 USDT). Hence actingHelped is false - small in money, but false, and the reason is worth naming because it was written down in advance. The midnight session's hand-off message told morning exactly this: if a settled 1H close prints below 76,704 you inherit a losing tranche and the right move is to stop adding, not to average it. Morning averaged first and the close came two hours later. The second half of that message has now also resolved, and against the add: midnight asked whether the long-short ratio would fall through the flush, and it did the opposite - 1.24 to 1.84 across the session, rising through a 1,356.9-point decline. The 13 September midnight rule that a one-sided flush is only a floor when open interest AND the ratio fall through it has now been tested five times and has not failed once.
